name: Voltface // Fracture Rave Bodysuit
description:
A seamless compression bodysuit by underground label Voltface, constructed from sound-reactive chromolux mesh layered over matte-black tensile base fabric. The chromolux layer pulses visible color — violet to acid green — in direct response to bass frequencies, creating moving bloom patterns across the torso and thighs. At rest, it reads as flat charcoal. Under a club sound system, the wearer becomes a living light source.

Cut high at the hip with a structured chest panel and open-back architecture. Neural port access collar allows BCI passthrough for sync'd light-pattern override — wearers with the right software can manually trigger color sequences. A Circuit-scene staple at underground raves in the old industrial tunnels beneath the MagLine grid.
functionality: Passive sound-reactive light display requires no power source — piezoelectric mesh converts sound pressure to light. BCI collar allows manual override for wearers with compatible implants. Compression fit provides mild thermal regulation.
what_it_says: I live for the underground, and my body is the show.
story_hooks: A Voltface suit starts responding to frequencies outside the audible range — something is broadcasting in the tunnel system.
Corporate IP enforcement is hunting the Voltface manufacturer for unlicensed chromolux use; the designer has gone dark.
A wearer's BCI override gets hijacked mid-rave, turning them into an unwilling signal beacon for someone watching the crowd.
